rows.falsifier: Empirical demonstration that neuro-symbolic error correction degrades metareasoning allocation efficiency without yielding error reduction benefits.
rows.reason: Supported by combined evidence on metareasoning partition problems and neuro-symbolic error correction.
rows.statement: Metareasoning resource allocation strategies can be coupled with neuro-symbolic verification to improve self-correction robustness under environmental distribution shifts.

rows.falsifier: Demonstration of a universal self-correction mechanism across diverse architectures without model-specific failure profiles.
rows.reason: Incorporating newly retrieved failure mode evidence into updated belief and safety verification profiles.
rows.statement: Automated reasoning models exhibit distinct safety failure profiles under adversarial pressure, preventing universal self-correction strategies.

rows.falsifier: Demonstration that mechanical verification state architectures and controlled update substrates fail to prevent drift or divergence across model invocations.
rows.reason: Evidence demonstrates that autonomous agents require explicit verification state architectures and substrate proportionality to maintain accountability across multi-turn trajectories.
rows.statement: Fresh model invocations can function as a singular, accountable process when bound by verifiable state architectures and substrate-appropriate update mechanisms.

rows.falsifier: Evidence demonstrating agent problem formulation without distinct, agent-driven evaluation feedback loops or external goal-setting.
rows.reason: Reinforced via updated review incorporating music generation and active inference findings regarding evaluation constraints.
rows.statement: Computational creativity frameworks require robust integration between formulation and evaluation components, supported by active inference and drift-diffusion mechanisms, for agents to autonomously navigate and identify novel, worthwhile problems.

rows.falsifier: Empirical demonstration that preference formation processes under misspecification consistently converge to unique, path-independent stable states.
rows.reason: Incorporating new structural mediation evidence (source-25f71adf01044c54) alongside general preference oracle frameworks further strengthens the confidence in path-dependent preference formation.
rows.statement: The inferential path-dependence of preference formation models under misspecification constrains the stability of autonomous agents, supported by general preference oracle frameworks and structural mediation analyses.

rows.falsifier: Development of an automated agent capable of identifying an internal logical paradox in its own base framework and initiating a valid, verified structural modification without external input or hard-coded triggers.
rows.reason: Synthesis of current project evidence shows that agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] excel at falsification within defined bounds, while ethics-based auditing literature [source-f26a645e047847a2] highlights the continued necessity for external governance to ensure normative consistency.
rows.statement: Current automated meta-reasoning frameworks operate strictly within fixed methodological parameters and lack the reflexive capacity to autonomously revise their foundational epistemic assumptions or procedural definitions without external intervention.
